passages.text: In rugby union, a try is worth five points, a conversion two, a penalty goal three, a drop goal three and a penalty try seven. A try is scored by grounding the ball in the opponent’s in-goal area, and the scoring team then attempts a conversion kick, taken in line with where the try was scored. Penalty goals are kicked after the opposition commits a penalty offense, and drop goals are scored by drop kicking the ball over the crossbar in open play. A penalty try is awarded when foul play prevents a probable try and needs no conversion. Rugby league scores differently, with four-point tries, two-point penalty goals and one-point field goals. Many union competitions also award bonus points in league tables for scoring four or more tries or losing narrowly. Rulebook note: Laws referenced here follow World Rugby’s Laws of the Game for rugby union, which sets scoring values. Rugby league, sevens and domestic competitions can differ, especially in bonus point systems and league scoring, and some competitions trial variations, so check the current rules for your competition.
